text:
Alex R: Heads-up — several customer restores failed around 02:10 UTC with KMS AccessDenied when trying to decrypt snapshots. Putting this here in case it's related to yesterday's cleanup job.
Maria G: Which customers? any common storage class or lifecycle rule?
Alex R: t-142 and t-188 so far. Snapshots show storage-class transition to GLACIER and a missing 'cmk-id' metadata tag on the object. Backup-agent v2.1.3 uploaded them.
Dinesh K: That sounds like the lifecycle cleanup lambda that strips tags when consolidating archives. We patched a similar edge-case but maybe not this path.
Ellie S: oncall-bot created incident INC-2026-432 (assigning to eng-security).
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-432 created and assigned to #eng-security. Priority P2.
Maria G: Quick CloudTrail check: there are repeated kms:Decrypt AccessDenied events correlated to the S3 object keys. Example query we used:
Maria G: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-22T01:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-22T03:00:00Z```
Alex R: Error from restore job: "AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh"
Dinesh K: Root cause hypothesis: lifecycle job removed the CMK pointer tag -> when object moved, backup-uploader's IAM path that relies on tag-based condition stopped matching -> no kms:Decrypt grant for that object -> restore fails.
InfraBot: Detected recent deploy: lifecycle-lambda v1.8.4 rolled out 2026-03-21T23:58Z to prod.
Maria G: Mitigation (short-term): recreate a grant for backup-uploader role against the CMK so restores can proceed while we fix metadata.
Alex R: Temporary create-grant command we ran successfully for one customer:
Alex R: ```bash
aws kms create-grant \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader \
  --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey \
  --name temp-restore-grant-1773334444
```
Dinesh K: That works but grants are ephemeral and our prune process will remove them after TTL. Need longer TTL or different approach.
Ellie S: Action items for incident: 1) Apply temporary grants for impacted tenants (Alex/Dinesh) 2) Disable the lifecycle tag-prune step (Maria) 3) Patch lifecycle-lambda to preserve 'cmk-id' or write CMK id into object metadata on transition (Dinesh) 4) Add audit alerts for when objects lose cmk metadata (Maria).
Maria G: Also adding: increase CloudTrail retention for kms:CreateGrant/RetireGrant events to 90 days and add an alert on unexpected RetireGrant activity.
Alex R: I'm pushing a diagnostics script to the incident runbook that enumerates objects missing cmk metadata and attempts a dry-run re-grant:
Alex R: ```python
# pseudo
for key in list_missing_cmk(bucket, prefix):
    print(key, "missing cmk tag")
    # show last uploader principal from object tagging/Audit
```
Dinesh K: I'll open a PR to lifecycle-lambda to add tag-preserve option + unit tests. Also will change the grant-prune job to ignore grants named temp-restore-* for 48h.
Ellie S: Can we add a defensive RBAC rule so only a specific operator svcacct can retire grants? We should tie retire permission to an approval workflow.
Maria G: Yes — change kms:RetireGrant and kms:CreateGrant scope in the policy to require a ticket context tag (we can enforce via IAM condition: aws:RequestTag/IncidentId).
Alex R: Postmortem notes to collect: timeline of lifecycle-lambda deploy -> objects moved -> missing tag -> failed restores; counts per tenant; list of manually created grants; audit entries for grant deletion.
InfraBot: Runbook reminder: "If widespread, escalate to SRE lead and rotate CMK if suspect compromise".
Dinesh K: I'll take lead on the patch, ETA for PR by EOD. Maria, can you add the CloudTrail alert rule and update the runbook?
Maria G: Yep, adding alert and runbook update now. Will also schedule a short sweep to reapply grants for impacted objects.
Ellie S: Thanks — keep updates in this thread and tag @oncall when mitigation complete. :white_check_mark:
